description: Resource-aware admission knobs for terminal_worker.py, consumed by tools/strategy_farm/resource_scheduler.py. Kill switch QM_RESOURCE_SCHEDULER (default off) must be truthy for any of this to take effect; with it off the worker's legacy claim/drain behaviour runs unchanged. All defaults here reproduce the pre-existing thresholds so activation is a pure staged rollout.

notes.heavy_reservation_gb: A candidate at/above this launch reservation is a heavy job that may require the exclusive pre-drain. Matches terminal_worker DRAIN_WINDOW_MIN_RESERVATION_GB (24 GB): two-leg metal/index and 44 GB single-index/heavy-multisymbol.
notes.fit_post_reservation_floor_gb: Free RAM that must remain AFTER a candidate's reservation for it to be considered a fit. Matches terminal_worker RAM_MIN_FREE_GB (14 GB).
notes.quiet_window_max_active_cells: A heavy candidate may open a pre-drain only when strictly fewer than this many cells are active fleet-wide. Directive: heavy jobs run in quieter windows / with reduced worker concurrency.
notes.head_window_candidates: Number of claimable head-window rows the worker surveys for a fitting smaller job before letting a heavy row arm a pre-drain. Widens the legacy top-3 preflight window (directive §12: replace simplistic queue ordering with resource-aware scheduling).
notes.heavy_starvation_max_wait_minutes: A heavy candidate continuously suppressed for at least this long is allowed to open a pre-drain regardless of fill, so heavy work never starves. Bounded and logged.
notes.frontier_weight: Value = priority + frontier_weight * frontier_gate. Default 0.0 keeps priority as today's sole ranking key; raise to prefer the highest-leverage frontier band among equally-fitting candidates. Facts-only ranking; never a verdict.
